note: Per bench, runtime and scenario: v1 cost over its raw twin's, the median of 3 interleaved pass medians (k=3, rounds held to 2.6 s, SPREAD_TOLERANCE 0.5; bit 21 k-pass), pooled from every CI run of bench code identical to cde0788 (24 runs: the six k=3 records at 5f2942e, the cde0788/e543a8b/a3fb58d/ea93db8 pushes, and the bref records at e543a8b and ea93db8; a3fb58d's and ea93db8's pushes and one record printed 19 of 27 lines, their 19 pooled; runs below). Ceiling rule (bit 21, both baselines): per scenario, fit log(ratio) (mean m, sample sd s), sigma_upper = s * sqrt((n-1)/chi2_0.10,n-1), z = Phi^-1(1 - 0.02/G) with G = 26 gated scenarios, ceiling = max(worst x 1.10, exp(m + z*sigma_upper)); baseline the median; catches = ceiling / baseline. Summed fitted per-run false-red probability 0.95% (budget 2%). Leave-one-out backtest (ceilings re-fitted per fold): 1 of 24 runs reds, 40991615047 itself (stream-1mb 2.08 against 2.024 from the other 23), an outlier the log-normal fit does not predict; its ceiling here is its floor, 2.08 x 1.1. A ratio cancels runner speed, not CPU microarchitecture, and GitHub hands out several CPU models (EPYC 7763, 9V45, 9V74, Xeon 8573C, 6973P-C seen), so a scenario whose level differs by model carries a reason naming its per-model levels and its catch on the lowest. A same-runner A/B gate (head vs a pinned base commit) replaces these ceilings next. A reportOnly scenario is printed and never fails the run. No retry: a red with v1 unchanged is answered by a re-record under this rule, never a rerun.
